images.after: How to judge whether a niche still has room
images.title: Four checks before you buy a domain
images.alt: Four steps to judge an affiliate niche: read what ranks, confirm programs pay enough, be honest about your knowledge, and check purchase frequency and price.
images.caption: Together these take about an afternoon. If a niche fails the first two, change the niche.

items.title: Read what already ranks
items.text: Outdated or vague top results are an opening. Big publishers mean narrow the topic.

items.title: Confirm programs pay enough
items.text: Check the commission rate, cookie window and payout threshold in each program's terms.

items.title: Be honest about what you know
items.text: Write twenty buyer questions. Can you answer most without looking anything up?

items.title: Check how often people buy
items.text: Repeat purchases or subscriptions support a steadier business. Price matters too.

images.after: Two things to set up from the first post
images.title: Set these up from the first post
images.alt: Two cards: disclose commissions clearly and close to the recommendation, and start an email list early.
images.caption: Disclosure is a legal expectation, and a list is an audience a ranking change can't take away.

items.title: Disclose your commissions
items.text: Clearly and conspicuously, close to the recommendation, as the FTC expects.

items.title: Start an email list
items.text: The one audience a ranking change can't take from you.
